The Bucs may or may not get Baker Mayfield back for this contest, but it will be a heated rivalry game regardless. It will also be crucial for the Buccaneers to cut into Carolina's division lead, so it could be a tough game regardless of how the two teams are perceived right now. What are the experts saying? Panthers vs. Buccaneers Week 7 NFL expert picks Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) plays against the Philadelphia Eagles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has not once picked the Panthers to win, and they've proved him wrong thrice. This time, though, he's going with the surging Panthers, although he's still not predicting a big performance. CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has not once picked the Panthers to win, and they've proved him wrong thrice. This time, though, he's going with the surging Panthers, although he's still not predicting a big performance. Prisco picked a one-point Panthers win, saying, "The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around." His CBS colleague John Breech is also picking the Panthers, but he's taking them by a field goal. Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff is picking a Panthers win, 24-16, betting on the Bryce Young-led offense to continue clicking at home. SI's Ian MacMillan isn't buying any of what the Panthers are doing, and he's picking the Buccaneers to upset them in Charlotte. "Time to sell high on [the Panthers]. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face... I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. away.headline: Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield back, rule out three starters
away.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game looking to rebound from a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay reason to be optimistic, but the absences of Egbuka, Goedeke, and Winfield will force the team to adjust on both sides of the ball. home.headline: Bryce Young, Panthers Defense Ripped by NFL Fans After Blowout Loss to Bucs in Baker's Injury Return
home.blurb: Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers were off to a solid start this season, but had some of their weaknesses exposed against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Young struggled in the 43-13 loss to the Bucs, throwing for just 163 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions on 14-of-27 passing. Unfortunately for Young and the Panthers' offense, they got little help from the defense. While Baker Mayfield had just 64 passing yards and a touchdown in his first game back since Week 3, Tampa Bay rushed for 258 yards and three touchdowns. Bucky Irving led the charge with 106 yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries. While the Panthers came into Sunday's matchup 3-2, their run defense had been inconsistent at best. They gave up 291 yards to the Chicago Bears in Week 1 but had success against top running backs like Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs. Carolina will need to be more consistent in keeping the ground game controlled if it wants to win the division and reach the playoffs again. As for Young, he came into the matchup against the Bucs ranking inside the top 10 in passing yards, touchdowns and interceptions, continuing to build off a career season in 2025. Clearly, Tampa Bay's defense rattled him, and he looked more like the rookie version of himself.

With Lamar Jackson officially ruled out due to an ankle injury, my Bengals vs. Ravens prediction backs Cincinnati to capitalize in today's pivotal AFC North showdown. Fresh off their bye week, the Bengals head to M&T Bank Stadium as 1.5-point road favorites, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Baltimore's quarterback situation opens the door for some intriguing trading opportunities, and my latest NFL picks target value across the moneyline, anytime touchdown, and completions markets this afternoon. TOP Pick Bengals vs Ravens prediction today: Bengals moneyline Editor's note: Jackson has now officially been ruled out and will miss his third straight game. Even though I gave them out at +2.5 earlier this week , I'm still willing to trade the Cincinnati Bengals 51% moneyline, up to 53% , against the Baltimore Ravens . Lamar Jackson has been limited in practice all week after missing the past two games, so there is no way he'll be 100% Sunday if he plays at all. An injured Lamar weakens Baltimore's offense , especially its ground game, because he's less likely to run, which is his biggest skill. Jackson averaged only 20.1 rushing yards per game when he returned from injury last season, and the Ravens missed the playoffs. Meanwhile, Cincinnati enters off a bye with a much cleaner injury situation . Since 2024, Baltimore is 1-5 against the spread (ATS) with a rest disadvantage and a -4.8 spread differential. For a straight-up pick on every game, see our NFL moneyline picks for Week 7 . Bengals vs Ravens combo This combo makes sense if Cincinnati turns the game into a Joe Burrow -controlled grind instead of asking its rushing attack to carry the offense. I want the Bengals living in manageable down-and-distance situations, stacking first downs, and forcing Baltimore to defend long possessions. That naturally gives Burrow more chances to pile up completions while increasing the odds that Ja'Marr Chase eventually finishes one of those drives in the end zone. The other side of the script matters, too. If Baltimore's offense is less explosive than usual, Cincinnati can stay patient and keep leaning on what Burrow does best. Give me Burrow moving the chains, Chase cashing in near the goal line, and the Bengals hanging around long enough to finish the job. Cincinnati may have to lean more heavily on Burrow's arm in this matchup. The Bengals rank 27th in yards per rush, while Baltimore is ninth in yards per rush allowed, making the passing game the cleaner path to points. And if Burrow is throwing near the goal line, Chase is obviously his first look. Chase has eight touchdowns in 10 career games against Baltimore and leads Cincinnati with four touchdown catches this season. Some receivers can be schemed out of games. Chase usually isn't one of them. For more touchdown props, see our NFL anytime touchdown picks for Week 7 . He's also been dinking and dunking more, ranking 24th in intended air yards per attempt . That style fits this prop perfectly. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nikhil Mehta Sun, October 25, 2026 at 3:15 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's almost time for the Ravens' Week 7 matchup with the Bengals! Here are Baltimore Beatdown's last-minute predictions: Like the Falcons, the Bengals seem like an especially bad matchup for the Ravens. Baltimore's offensive line finally has their best five, but it is still Cam Jurgens' first game snapping to Tyler Huntley in a new offense. And he has to deal with Dexter Lawrence. On defense, well, we've seen this movie before Joe Burrow to Ja'Marr Chase for first down or a touchdown at all of the worst moments. But I picked against the Ravens in Atlanta, and Derrick Henr X-factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Huntley needs a big, quarterback-friendly target that he can trust with contested catches, whether he's trying to push the ball downfield or hit a hot read against the blitz. Lane has proven he can operate in traffic over the middle with a good feel for picking up the requisite yards for a first down. This feels like a good week for his first regular-season touchdown. Score prediction: Ravens 24, Bengals 21 With no Lamar Jackson, the Ravens' offense will again be limited. Therefore, the onus will be on their defense to carry the load, as they did last week, but forcing turnovers may be necessary. If the Ravens' defense can come up with a takeaway or two and give their offense a short-field to work with, that could make a huge difference. Their pass rush against Joe Burrow needs to be relentless and effective to disrupt the Bengals' lethal passing attack. X-factor: Cam Jurgens. Expecting great results from Jurgens in his first game as a Raven, coming off a concussion, may be unfair. However, the Ravens will need him to hold his own in a tough matchup against DT Dexter Lawrence. If Jurgens is overwhelmed in one-on-one matchups with Lawrence, the latter might wreck any chance of offensive success for the Ravens. Score prediction: Ravens 17, Bengals 24 Kevin McNelis Last week wasn't pretty, and while they get multiple pieces a little healthier, they're now down Tavius Robinson and still without Lamar Jackson. It doesn't bode well as they face a well-rounded Bengals team that's given the secondary fits even when the Ravens have managed to win against them over the past few seasons. Derrick Henry's success was limited last week, and maybe the offense can mix it up a little bit more than they did last week, but they're going to need the defense to make some plays and set up short fields if they want to have any hope of winning this game. The next guys up in Zion Young, Mike Green, and Keondre Jackson filling in for Jaylinn Hawkins can prove that they deserve bigger spots by stepping up and making big plays in the expanded roles. X-factor: I'd even venture to give Keondre Jackson my X-factor player for this game based on how important the back end of the defense is going to be as they face the Bengals receivers. My heart has hope, but my head feels like it knows where this game goes. Score prediction: Bengals 27, Ravens 16 Any game without Lamar Jackson will be tough to win for the Ravens, but a divisional matchup with a Bengals team fresh off a bye week is an especially difficult hurdle to overcome with a backup quarterback. If Baltimore wants to pull off the upset with Tyler Huntley on Sunday, then getting the run game going with Derrick Henry is absolutely paramount to sustaining offensive success. Henry was bottled up against the Browns a week ago and Huntley was unable to carry the load with his arm. If the Ravens can get a classic Henry performance, then they should have a real chance against the Bengals. Baltimore's defense has played better in recent weeks, but Sunday will present their toughest challenge yet with Joe Burrow throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. The Ravens' secondary has done a good job of eliminating explosive plays down the field, but Chase and Higgins will put that to the test. I predict a respectable fight from the Ravens, but without Jackson, I do not foresee Baltimore's offense having enough juice to keep up with Cincinnati's passing attack over the course of four quarters. X-factor: Trey Hendrickson. Hendrickson is surely chomping at the bit to get back at his former team on Sunday. While the secondary will need to be at their best, an effective pass rush would go a long way in preventing Burrow from having a field day through the air. Score prediction: Bengals 27 Ravens 20

Most national analysts picked Cincinnati at M&T Bank Stadium while Lamar Jackson was still questionable, and with Jackson ruled out, the line has flipped to Bengals by about 2.5 . That fits the tone of our bold predictions for Sunday . The Ravens' own team site counted 36 of 47 pundits picking the Bengals. Here's how the major outlets see it. Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) exchanges words with Baltimore Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins (2) in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 15 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Baltimore Ravens at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Dec. 14, 2025. The Bengals were shut out, 24-0. Six of seven CBS Sports experts took Cincinnati straight up, with Ryan Wilson the lone Ravens pick, on the CBS expert board . John Breech has the Bengals winning 27-24, siding with the healthier quarterback in his CBS Sports picks . The Bengals improved to 3-2 on the season with a 31-24 win on the road.USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Four of five NFL.com analysts picked Cincinnati: Jeremy Bergman (27-24), Gennaro Filice (25-20), Bobby Kownack (28-27) and Dan Parr (27-25). Brooke Cersosimo was the lone holdout at 28-25 Ravens. Filice leaned on the Lawrence trade . "This is exactly why the Bengals traded the No. 10 overall pick for Dexter Lawrence," Filice wrote in NFL.com's Week 7 picks , citing Cincinnati's league-leading 23% stuff rate. He also warned that "even if it's Tyler Huntley, Baltimore can still pound the rock with Derrick Henry." Sports Illustrated and The Athletic Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) talks with head coach Zac Taylor during an official review in the third quarter of the NFL Week 7 game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 24, 2021. The Bengals moved into the top of the AFC North with a 41-17 win over the Ravens. Cincinnati Bengals At Baltimore Ravens Week 7 SI's staff went 5-3 for Cincinnati , with Albert Breer and Conor Orr among the five. Jeff Zrebiec and Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic both took the Bengals. "I think the Ravens will have a hard time stopping a fresh and healthy Bengals team and Cincinnati will win," Zrebiec wrote for The Athletic . Dehner liked the Bengals "especially if Jackson can't go or is limited in his mobility." Bleacher Report and Pro Football Talk Oct 18, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (4) runs the ball under pressure from Cleveland Browns safety Grant Delpit (9) in the first quarter at Huntington Bank Field. Bleacher Report's staff went 4-3 for Baltimore against the spread when the Ravens were laying 2.5, and Brad Gagnon, who picked the Bengals to win the AFC North, is among the four. Gary Davenport wrote that "even if he sits, the Ravens are the pick here," pointing to Zac Taylor's 3-4 record off a bye. "The Ravens get after Joe Burrow, lean on Derrick Henry and win by a field goal," he wrote for Bleacher Report . Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk took Baltimore 28-24, though his case began with "The Ravens need Lamar Jackson to return." That's a lot of national support for a team Burrow says isn't respected like it was . "We want to be 4-2 and controlling our own destiny, and it really starts this week," Burrow told reporters this week . With Huntley starting, Jackson's ankle could swing more than one game in the division. away.headline: Lamar Jackson Fires Back at NFL Insider Over Inaccurate Injury Report Ahead of Bengals Clash
away.blurb: Jackson has been absent in the last two games. After sustaining an injury in a Week 4 game against the Tennessee Titans, he has not played a single minute. He has now come out to speak against a report about his return. Rapoport has not issued a statement in regards to Jackson's comments. The player is still listed as questionable for the next game against the Cincinnati Bengals, and has talked about the situation. Lamar Jackson talks about potential return Jackson has been participating in limited practice sessions. While he is still listed as questionable, the quarterback is doing his best to recover. He talked about his injury situation in the press conference, and revealed that he does not know when he would return. He said , "I can't call it right now. I still [have] got a grace period, so we'll see, but hopefully. I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now." He added, "I don't have a number, but I don't feel like I have to be 100. If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, [then] that's it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. picks.headline: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants might have a winning record (3-2-1) right now and lead the NFC East. But let’s be honest. Aside from their dominant Week 1 showing against the Dallas Cowboys, have the Giants really looked as good as their record suggests? We’re talking about a team where the phrase “A win’s a win” applies. The Giants barely beat the Tennessee Titans, 12-7, in Week 3. They also had to fight back in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, who led 24-19 at one point. The tie against the Commanders? That one was a gift. If Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn don’t have that brain blip, the Commanders likely win, despite the Giants roaring back from a 19-6 deficit. And last week? We’re sorry, but the Giants had no business losing to the New Orleans Saints as badly as they did. And again, make no mistake: the Giants lost that game because they were their own worst enemy, as shown by the sloppy play they put on film. But it’s funny how the football gods work. The Giants, regardless of what they do against the Houston Texans this week, will remain in first place in the division. They have a chance, albeit a difficult one, to get back to looking like the team they were in Week 1, even though they’ve since lost a lot of key personnel, all of whom played in that win: quarterback Jaxson Dart, returner/receiver Braxton Berrios, outside linebacker Brian Burns, and inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. So what’s the goal this week if the Giants want to pull off an upset win over the Texans on the road? “We’ve been practicing well the last few weeks,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think practice has been improving every single week, which is the mark of a team that has got a chance to do something. You’ve got to keep improving. “So, we are on track to do that. I’m looking forward to it showing up in terms of consistency. If we’ve been anything, we’ve been inconsistent.” It’s really that simple. The question is, will the Giants finally find the consistency that’s eluded them since that Week 1 game? Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans The Texans might be on a roll, having won their last two games, but they still have a few flaws that could work to the Giants’ advantage. For one, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 27th in the PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating metric. The unit has allowed 71 quarterback pressures, tied for third-most in the league. Left tackle Aireontae Ersery has allowed 20 quarterback pressures, per PFF, tied for fourth-most in the league among left tackles. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has turned up the heat on opposing quarterbacks in recent weeks. This year, opposing quarterbacks have completed only 54.1% of their pass attempts against the Giants’ blitz, the fourth-lowest completion rate in the league. Of course, the key is for the Giants to stop the run, something they haven’t done consistently in recent weeks. So we’ll see if Wilson’s calling out his defensive players for not running to the ball lights a fire underneath them. Offensively, the Giants need to get their running game going, and the hope is that switching to quarterback J.J. McCarthy will help. This more mobile quarterback will discourage the Texans from loading up the box and start accounting for McCarthy as a runner. More importantly, McCarthy’s ability to scramble away from trouble could help the Giants’ ailing offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and, if he plays, Jermaine Eluemunor, against that Texans pass rush. Per Next Gen Stats, since 2025, McCarthy has scrambled 19 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns, a 9.7 yards-per-carry average, which is a league high among quarterbacks with a minimum of 15 carries. If McCarthy can buy time, he stands a chance at connecting with receiver Malik Nabers or tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have been the most frequently targeted players on offense for the Giants over the last few weeks. Why the Giants Will Lose to the Texans I touched on it a bit above, but I’ll say it again here. The Giants have to stop the run. Texans’ top running back, David Montgomery, has been sidelined with a groin injury, but Woody Marks has stepped up in his place. Marks is an explosive running back who has averaged almost four yards per rush over the last two weeks. He also has six catches for 47 yards over that span. The Giants’ run defense? Not good at all. Big Blue has allowed opponents 135.5 rushing yards per game this year, and their 5.0 yards per carry allowed is the second-worst average in the league. If the Giants can’t stuff Marks and the Texans’ running game, it won’t matter what pass-rush plan they have this week. And until the unit shows it has cleaned up the missed tackles (13 last week, seven against the run per PFF), that aspect of the game will remain the team’s Achilles heel. At the start of the season, I had this game down as a loss and nothing — not even the Texans’ 2-4 record or the Giants’ 3-2-1 start — has changed my mind. The Texans have been coming into their own lately, and the Giants, aside from their Week 1 win over Dallas, have barely gotten by in their other wins and in their tie against Washington. The Giants will fight — that much I am certain of — and I hope this doesn’t turn into the ugly rout that I fear it could become. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. away.headline: Giants’ Cam Skattebo thankful for bye week after late injury scare on heroic OT run
away.blurb: It appeared that Skattebo could have been vulnerable to the ball being punched out of his arms if he had been caught from behind by the Houston defense. Skattebo had a solid return to the Giants offense after he had been held without a carry in New York’s Week 6 game against the New Orleans Saints. He had 17 carries for 124 yards and he scored a touchdown. He averaged 7.3 yards per carry and punished the Houston defense with his hard-hitting style. Skattebo will have a chance to rest and recover from his hamstring issue since the Giants are headed into their bye week and won’t return until Week 9 when they travel to Philadelphia. Related: Giants’ Cam Skattebo pulls out backflip after mowing down Texans defenders with revenge game TD The New York Giants came through on the road in Week 7 with a 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans. The Giants won the game when Devin Singletary sprinted 30 yards down the sideline and made it into the endzone. While Singletary delivered the winning touchdown, fellow RB Cam Skattebo set up the score when he rumbled 42 yards on the preceding play. Skattebo took the handoff from J.J. McCarthy, took advantage of solid blocking by the New York offensive line and sprinted into the clear. It appeared that Skattebo could have run for an additional 10 yards on the play, but he slid down at the 30. The running back said he decided to avoid being caught from behind because he said he “ felt something ” in the back of his hamstring and wanted to avoid an injury. Running back returns with determination Skattebo’s running game provided excellent support for QB J.J. McCarthy, who was making his first start for the Giants. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. He did not throw a TD pass, but he kept it clean on the interception side of the ledger. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Luka Dončić drops 52 on Jazz as Lakers stay unbeaten TRENDING Chiefs vs. Seahawks updates New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries
away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. Adebo has been on IR since Week 2

home.blurb: Giants-Texans final injury report: Tremaine Edmunds out, Micah McFadden in - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Giants-Texans final injury report: Tremaine Edmunds out, Micah McFadden in With Edmunds out, fifth-year linebacker and former starter Micah McFadden will get the starting nod. "If I get to go out there and play and start and do what I've gotten to do before, I'm excited," McFadden told Big Blue View earlier this week. McFadden was a full-time starter for the Giants in 2023 and 2024. In Game 1 last season, McFadden suffered a foot injury that kept him out for the remainder of the season. He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. "Whenever you're used to something, you've had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don't get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it's tough, but I think it's just about staying present," McFadden said. "This game is a week-to-week basis, and obviously I had a pretty upsetting first week last year, and I learned a lot through that process, though. A lot of gratitude to be healthy and just to be able to play again, and I think that's what I found most throughout these past six weeks is just, just finding gratitude in whatever situation I'm in." The Giants designated cornerback Paulson Adebo to return this week, and it looks like he could be activated before Sunday's game. With starting cornerback Greg Newsome II still in concussion protocol and ruled out, there could be immediate snaps for Adebo vs. the Texans. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. away.headline: Pat Surtain injury: Latest updates for Broncos cornerback
away.blurb: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain went down with a non-contact ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers . He was ruled out in the third quarter. After sitting out Sunday's game, Pat Surtain told the Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson that he wasn't really close to playing in Week 7. When asked if he could return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, Surtain said, "Possibly." Broncos CB Pat Surtain is inactive and will miss his third straight game. However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport tweeted on Sunday that " there's a good chance " Surtain will be able to return against the Chiefs in Week 8. Broncos CB Pat Surtain questionable for Week 7 Denver's injury report for Sunday's game against Arizona has cornerback Pat Surtain officially listed as questionable . If he can't play, Jahdae Barron will likely be the next man up. Despite returning to practice on Wednesday, Pat Surtain seems more likely to return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, according to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video . We'll see how the week goes for PS2. Pat Surtain might not return in Week 7 In an updated report on Pat Surtain's status, James Palmer of Prime Video clarified that PS2's injury was not a non-contact injury — it actually happened one play before the cornerback went down on the field. Palmer also reported that " [i]t might be tough " for Surtain to return to action in Week 7, suggesting PS2 might be more likely to return in Week 8. Pat Surtain ruled out for Week 6; there's hope for possible Week 7 return Pat Surtain has been ruled out for a Thursday Night Football clash with the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, but there is hope he might be able to return against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, according to KUSA-TV's Mike Klis . Pat Surtain avoids IR; ruled out for Week 5 ESPN's Adam Schefter said on Altitude Sports Radio that his guess is that Pat Surtain will land on injured reserve , which would rule the cornerback out for at least four games. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Pat Surtain is expected to miss time, but it's not believed to be season-ending. "You hope it is just a couple weeks, maybe it ends up in an IR stint, but not expected to be season-ending," Rapoport said . If Surtain is placed on injured reserve, he would have to sit out at least four games. Broncos CB Pat Surtain ruled out Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), who were both originally listed as questionable to return, have been announced as ruled out for the rest of today's game. Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron are the two outside cornerbacks with Ja'Quan McMillian playing in the slot. Behind them on Denver's depth chart , the Broncos also have Kris Abrams-Draine. With PS2 sidelined, the team is down to four healthy cornerbacks on the active roster. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals’ Defensive Problems Return Against Struggling Broncos
away.blurb: Arizona Cardinals' Defensive Problems Return Against Struggling Broncos The Cardinals' defense came into Sunday's matchup facing one of the NFL's worst offenses statistically. Then, they allowed at least 30 points for the fifth time in 2026. The trend of allowing at least 30 points outside of SoFi Stadium continues for another week as Arizona once again goes back to the drawing board to try to figure out what went wrong. Unlock the latest Heavy on AZ Cardinals news — direct to your inbox. In Sunday's loss to the Denver Broncos , the Arizona Cardinals once again allowed at least 30 points at their home venue. For a while, it looked like Arizona would keep Bo Nix and Co. in check. Arizona went into the half trailing 13-6 before RJ Harvey scored on a 52-yard touchdown pass from Nix. Once again, the Cardinals ‘ defense allowed an explosive play through the air. Something that has been yet another recurring theme for this defense. After a touchdown from tight end Trey McBride brought the Cardinals back to a seven-point deficit, the Broncos responded with another scoring drive. The big play of the drive? A 47-yard pass to Marvin Mims Jr. to set up first-and-goal. Arizona Cardinals Defense Collapsed Against A Struggling Offense The Broncos came into this Week 7 matchup averaging 252 yards of total offense. They gained 377 yards on Sunday afternoon. Besides the 52-yard strike to Harvey and the 47-yard pass to Mims, Arizona also allowed completions of 27 and 20 yards. Nix also broke free for a 62-yard run for a touchdown. Two Broncos touchdowns came as a result of explosive plays. A third came thanks to an explosive play setting them up for first-and-goal. Denver also tacked on three field goals to get its 30 points. Denver had reached the 30-point mark just once before they put up 30 on the Cardinals. That occurred in Week 3 vs. the Los Angeles Rams . Opposing defenses held Denver to under 20 points in three of their first six games. Week 7 also marked the second time the Broncos made it over the 300-yard threshold in a game, per their Pro-Football-Reference page. With the way Denver torched the Arizona Cardinals' defense on Sunday, it shows that Nick Rallis and Co. still have a lot of problems to fix. Cardinals Must Find Answers Before Week 8 The Cardinals' defense had a chance to string together stellar back-to-back performances. Now that their Week 7 matchup is in the books, Week 8 isn't getting any easier. They will face a Dallas Cowboys offense that has crossed the 300-plus-yard threshold in five of their first six games. If there is a silver lining, it is that the Cardinals' offense may enjoy a better outing, considering the state that the Cowboys' own defense has been in. away.headline: Jaylen Waddle injury update as Broncos WR leaves game vs Cardinals
away.blurb: The Broncos announced Waddle suffered a chest injury during Sunday's game against the Cardinals. He was deemed "questionable" to return but did not see the field for the remainder of Denver's 30-16 win after exiting with 4:$5 remaining in regulation. Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle suffered an apparent injury late in his team's Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals . Waddle's injury occurred after the receiver tried to take an end-around hand-off. The 27-year-old fumbled the hand-off and had to dive on it behind the line of scrimmage to ensure the Broncos would not lose possession. Waddle landed on top of the ball but then had Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat land on top of him almost immediately after. Waddle remained down in pain following the tackle and appeared to be reaching for his shoulder or chest. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. Waddle eventually exited the field and headed to the blue medical tent for further evaluation. He was later seen walking to the locker room, alongside members of Denver's athletic training staff. Sean Payton did not provide an update on Waddle's status following the game. He did, however, refer to the play on which Waddle was hurt as a "dumb" and "awful" call by himself. "I know better," Payton told reporters , referencing a similar call he made in a 2008 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers while he was coaching the New Orleans Saints. "Every once in a while you fall in love with a play." Before exiting the game, Waddle logged four catches for 48 yards. He did not have a rushing attempt; Bo Nix was charged with a fumble on his lone carry, and Waddle was credited with the recovery. away.headline: Broncos have 7 players on injured reserve going into Week 7
away.blurb: Four of those players — wide receiver Pat Bryant ( ankle ), running back Jonah Coleman ( ankle ), offensive tackle Frank Crum and tight end Caleb Lohner — are on short-term injured reserve, which means they are eligible to return after four games (although Lohner is expected to be out until at least mid-season ). Coleman is eligible to return from IR this week , and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss might be a candidate for IR after he was spotted using a walking boot and crutches over the weekend. Another player, offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo , is on the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. He is also eligible to return after four games. home.headline: Is Budda Baker playing today? The latest on the Cardinals S
home.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals take on the Denver Broncos on Sunday in Week 7, and one injury of note is with safety Budda Baker. He is listed officially as questionable on the final injury report of the week. Baker suffered a groin injury in practice last week. He played through on Sunday in the Cardinals' 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams , but it bothered him in practice this week. Baker did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, and he was a limited prarticipant in Friday's practice. While he is listed as questionable, he is expected to play. That was confirmed by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. He posted on X that Baker is expected to play . Saturday's roster moves also suggested that Baker would be good to go. Safety Andrew Wingard is out with a knee injury, and the Cardinals cut rookie safety Wydett Williams, leaving the only available safeties for Week 7 as Baker, Dadrion Taylor-Demerson and Kitan Grawford. What is the latest status for Baker? Baker has only missed practice time. He has played every one of the Cardinals' defensive snaps this season. The Packers, winners of three in a row, are coming off a 23-13 defeat of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Meanwhile, Detroit, which spent Week 6 on its bye, defeated the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, 45-21. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay. Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker. Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch. Packers 31, Lions 28 The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden. I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season. Lions 31, Packers 24 John Maakaron The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup. If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets. Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract. Emmett Matasovsky The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing. It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant. Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. The Lions, on fresh legs and with momentum, alongside a rowdy Ford Field crowd, take the win to open the second half of the season. Lions 31, Packers 27 Published 13 hours ago VITO CHIRCO Vito has covered the NFL and the Detroit Lions for the past five years. Has extensive reporting history of college athletics, the Detroit Tigers and Detroit Mercy Athletics. Chirco's work include NFL columns, analyzing potential Detroit Lions prospects coming out of college, NFL draft coverage and analysis of events occurring in the NFL. picks.blurb: Packers-Lions Prediction: Will Green Bay Beat Odds So It Can Beat Rivals? Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI DETROIT – One of the biggest games of the season for the Green Bay Packers comes with one of the biggest scheduling mismatches imaginable. The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest. Will it matter? Here are our predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Lions Prediction Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage. Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback. Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel. The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home. The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game. The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history. For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games. Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way. One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love? Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough? Furthermore, the Green Bay defense will line up without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures. “The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said. It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed. Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers. Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27. Bill’s Record: 3-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Lions Prediction The Packers have lost too many games like these in recent years, which have caused them to travel the long road in the postseason. In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field. Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender. In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined? Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers? That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod. Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31 Jacob’s Record: 3-3. Even with drops (bad) and interference penalties drawn (good), the Packers' Matthew Golden is having the biggest breakout season by a receiver in more than a decade. ⬇️ https://t.co/EsADb0e8gG Published 12 hours ago BILL HUBER Bill Huber, who has covered the Green Bay Packers since 2008, is the publisher of Packers On SI, a Sports Illustrated channel. With The News-Chronicle, he won several awards for his commentaries and page design. In 2008, he took over as editor of Packer Report Magazine, which was founded by Hall of Fame linebacker Ray Nitschke, and PackerReport.com. In 2019, he took over the new Sports Illustrated site Packer Central, which he has grown into one of the largest sites in the Sports Illustrated Media Group. After a 1-2 start to the season, the Pack have won three games in a row, dominating the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night in Week 6. Green Bay’s offense has been one of the more explosive passing games in the league, which is a concern for a short-handed Lions secondary that is dead last in the league in EPA/Play this season. Plus, Josh Jacobs is in line to make his 2026 debut for the Packers, the first time they’ll be close to full strength on the offensive side of the ball. Detroit (3-2) is looking to come out of the bye with a home win, and it’s been an elite offense with Jahmyr Gibbs and Goff leading the way. All four NFC North teams could make the playoffs this season, so head-to-head tiebreakers may loom large later on in 2026. All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, a fun way to help bettors decide on spread, total and moneyline bets. I’m also out to hit a couple exact scores in the 2026 campaign. This NFC North matchup is the highlight of the late slate on Sunday, as both teams are looking to get a leg up with everyone in this division over .500 through the first six-plus weeks of the season. Packers vs. Lions Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Detroit to come out of the bye with a win: We all know how bad the Lions' defense has been this season, but they're getting some reinforcement coming off their bye week. Their star safety, Brian Branch, is set to make his first start of the season since suffering an injury last year. While he may not be able to completely turn this defense around himself, his boost to their secondary can't be understated. All he has to do is help the Lions' defense force even just a few more punts, and if he can do that, Detroit is going to be in great shape. Their offense is one of the best in the league, ranking sixth in EPA per play and fifth in success rate. Green Bay has been a much better defensive team than the Lions this season, and the return of Josh Jacobs should help boost a running game that has been one of the worst in the league. While MacMillan is on the Lions to cover, I think this could be a high-scoring affair with the Packers’ big-play ability in the passing game. The Lions are dead last in the league in EPA/Play on defense and third on offense, hitting the OVER in all five of their games to date. I’ll bet on that trend continuing with Detroit coming off the bye. Final Score Prediction: Lions 30, Packers 27 Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. Cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) does not have a game status and will play. ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window * The Lions did not practice Wednesday; Practice participation designations for that day are based on estimations. news Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night news Packers list three questionable, two doubtful vs. Bears | Week 5 Injury Report DT Javon Hargrave (toe) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday news Packers rule out four, list two questionable vs. Buccaneers | Week 4 Injury Report OL Aaron Banks, Jacob Monk ruled out; LB Edgerrin Cooper questionable for Sunday Veteran linebacker won’t play Sunday after suffering injury at Thursday’s practice Wes Hodkiewicz packers.com senior writer Head Coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Friday morning that Franklin took a knee to his shin during a collision at practice Thursday. home.blurb: As for the Packers, offensive guard Aaron Banks, who hasn't played in any of the Green Bay's last four games, is back in the lineup. We already knew starting linebacker Zaire Franklin wouldn't be available after he got hurt in practice Friday, Oct. 23, according to Packers coach Matt LaFleur. As expected, safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) are active and set to make their season debuts. Branch hasn't played in a game since he went down in a win over the Dallas Cowboys last December. home.headline: Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire
home.blurb: Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire Skip to main content SI.COM Cooper, of course, is on injured reserve with a torn Achilles. Franklin suffered an injured shin at practice on Thursday and is out on the Packers’ final injury report. Franklin was the only player ruled out by LaFleur on the injury report. Left guard Aaron Banks, receiver Bo Melton, defensive tackle Jordon Riley and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste are questionable. Star safety Brian Branch said he’s “ready to roll” as he makes his debut following last season’s torn Achilles. Officially, he is questionable. “I’m really excited, to be honest,” he told reporters in Detroit. “Play the game that you love that you've been missing out for so long. To come back like this is a blessing to be able to play this game. I'm just going to execute [the game plan] and, if I execute, it's going to be a hell of a game.” Questionable: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), WR Bo Melton (back), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring). Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. Questionable: S Brian Branch (Achilles), C Cade Mays (wrist). Branch has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. DETROIT – There’s never a good time to play without your starting linebackers. That’s especially true for the Green Bay Packers, who will play without premier starter Edgerrin Cooper and defensive captain Zaire Franklin for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions. It’s not exactly ideal considering the Lions are second in the NFL in scoring, fourth in total offense and have a premier running back with Jahmyr Gibbs. “Unfortunate deal,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “That happens when you play football, especially the way our guys have been practicing.” Quarterback Jordan Love (back) and cornerback Brandon Cisse (stinger) are among those off the final injury report. Melton missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday but returned on Friday. Riley remains on injured reserve but just completed his second week of practice. Banks hasn’t played since his one and only game against the Jets in Week 2. St-Juste was inactive last week. “Big, stout physical D-lineman. Exactly what we need,” coach Matt LaFleur said of Riley before practice. As expected , unning back Josh Jacobs appears ready to make his debut after being removed from the exempt list this week. home.headline: Packers Get Good Injury News on Explosive WR Duo Before Lions Game
home.blurb: Watson was listed with an ankle injury, while Golden appeared with a shoulder issue. Both were estimated limited participants as Green Bay conducted a walkthrough rather than a full practice. The team's injury concerns extend beyond those two receivers, however. Love was also listed as limited Wednesday because of a back injury, while fellow wideout Savion Williams appeared with an ankle injury. The importance of having both receivers available becomes even clearer when considering what Detroit is preparing to defend. There's also the potential return of running back Josh Jacobs , who resumed practicing this week after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list. With the Packers visiting Detroit at Ford Field on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, LaFleur's latest update suggests Green Bay should have its top two passing-game weapons available for a pivotal divisional matchup.
