home.headline: Jordan Love, Christian Watson among Packers off injury report and set to play vs. Lions
home.blurb: Earlier this week, Packers quarterback Jordan Love told reporters he would be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed as limited on Wednesday with a back issue. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Savion Williams (ankle), and Matthew Golden (shoulder) are also off the injury report and are all set to play, despite being listed as limited all week. Guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), receiver Bo Melton (back), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackle Jordan Riley (Achilles) are all questionable. Head coach Matt LaFleur noted earlier on Friday that linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) is out after suffering an injury on Thursday . Well, anyone backing the Raiders in Week 7 has a lot more company, with a good chunk of the experts giving them a real shot against the Rams Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Covering the spread against Buffalo apparently buys a team some respect. The computer models still like the Rams comfortably, but some of the humans are far less sure, and a few of them switched sides from last week. Even the Raiders Wire staff is on board too, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 27-25. NFL.com's panel can barely agree Three of NFL.com's five analysts picked the Rams, with Jeremy Bergman at 24-17, Gennaro Filice at 27-24 and Dan Parr at 31-27. The other two went with the Raiders, and both picks come with a story. Bobby Kownack had the Bills hanging 35 points on the Raiders last week. Now he has the Raiders winning a 17-14 rock fight , which is quite a change of heart in seven days. Brooke Cersosimo has the Raiders by one at 25-24, and the Rams clearly gave her more to think about than she expected. "Of all the teams in the league, I would not have guessed the Rams would give me pause at this point in the season," Cersosimo wrote. She also has the game ending on a Raiders field goal in the final minute. Bleacher Report's experts traded seats The funniest twist came from Bleacher Report. Maurice Moton was the panel's lone Raiders backer last week, and this week he jumped to the Rams, while Gary Davenport, who doubted the Raiders against Buffalo, came over to their side. "Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo?" Davenport wrote. Moton expects the Rams to adjust without Davante Adams by leaning on their tight ends. The panel finished 4-3 in favor of the Raiders against a 4.5-point spread, with Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski joining Davenport. Pete Prisco and Mike Florio keep it tight CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Rams to win by a single point, 28-27, which is a polite way of taking the Raiders against the spread. "They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here," Prisco wrote. "But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders, who hang around." The rest of the CBS panel split 4-3 for the Rams against the spread, with Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg standing with Prisco. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Rams winning 26-23 and sees a season on the line for Los Angeles. "If the Rams get to five losses with 10 games left, they could be done," Florio wrote. The computers aren't buying it The models are far more confident than we (humans). Dimers gives the Rams a 70.8% chance to win with a 26-20 projection, and the Covers AI model has Los Angeles winning 27-20. Five of the seven human score predictions in this roundup land within three points, though. These experts expect another one-score game, and the Raiders have lost two of their last three games by a field goal. away.headline: Report: Rams are 'optimistic' Puka Nacua will play today vs. Raiders
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams listed Puka Nacua as questionable to play against the Las Vegas Raiders this week after he injured his calf in practice on Thursday. He was forced to exit practice early and did not participate on Friday, leading to a lot of speculation about whether he'll play in Sunday's game . Adam Schefter of ESPN reports the Rams are "optimistic" that Nacua will suit up and play today. Schefter noted that one source said, "as long as there aren't any setbacks, we feel good about him being available to play." Ian Rapoport of NFL Network added that Nacua will "work out today, but the hope is he is on the field." That's great news for the Rams, who are already without Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson on offense. Nacua missed two games earlier this season due to a hip/groin injury, so the hope is that he won't have to miss a third game in seven weeks. In just four games this season, Nacua has caught 37 passes for 417 yards and one touchdown. He also has a rushing touchdown. He led the NFL in receptions and receiving yards per game a season ago, earning first-team All-Pro honors and finishing third in the Offensive Player of the Year race. He didn’t rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email 🪄 Harry Houdini's great escapes ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. If they can do that, they will have a chance to score the upset. As the game nears, let's see who the experts believe will walk away with the win this weekend. "Walker leads the league with 665 rushing yards -- and that’s despite the fact that he’s played one fewer game than the next three leading rushers (Bijan Robinson, James Cook III and Derrick Henry), thanks to K.C.’s Week 5 bye. Meanwhile, the Seahawks have yet to finish a game with a 100-yard rusher, and their well-documented struggles on the ground are putting too much on Sam Darnold’s plate, as evidenced by the quarterback’s seven interceptions in the past four weeks." picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Seahawks: NFL Week 7 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Kansas City Chiefs are back in prime time this weekend, taking center stage at Lumen Field in a matter of hours against a feisty Seattle Seahawks squad that's still finding its way a bit after winning the Super Bowl earlier this calendar year. Don't let the home team's offensive struggles fool you, though, as this remains one of the premier clubs in the NFL. Head coach Mike Macdonald's group might have the game's best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seahawks' defense is in the conversation for being football's most elite unit once again. Kansas City has its work cut out for it in what could be a tough road game, but one thing this year's team has shown is an abundance of grit. Will Sunday Night Football be more of the same? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 7 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Between the Seahawks’ offensive inconsistencies and the Chiefs’ offensive injuries, this feels like a low-scoring, wire-to-wire affair between two teams with elite elements in some areas and significant questions in others. Ultimately, fitting the narrative of the week perfectly, Kenneth Walker should be the key to this game for both teams. Jordan Foote: Going into Seattle and securing a win is easily the toughest ask of the Chiefs through the first month-and-a-half of the season. The Seahawks' defense, even while banged up, is amazing. On the other side of the ball, however, there's next to no run game. That's had a negative impact on quarterback Sam Darnold, who also isn't sniffing the production he found a season ago. Week 7's tilt could go either way, but I'll side with the offense I believe in much more. Minus wideout Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore , look for this one to be a statement game for one or both of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III in hostile territory. Joshua Schulman: Kenneth Walker is set to return to face the franchise he won a Super Bowl with less than nine months ago, and he'll be looking to make his former team regret letting him walk. He and Jaxon Smith-Njigba headline one of the most exciting Sunday Night Football contests in recent memory. There's a generational quarterback in Patrick Mahomes squaring off against a generational defense that has picked up where it left off a season ago, despite the offense's inconsistencies. Seattle's slow start has actually placed it out of the playoff picture, and a home loss before another prime-time showdown against the Bears would be disastrous. I think the Seahawks understand the importance of this matchup and will take advantage of their 10 days of rest. Given the Chiefs' shaky kicking game and a lack of proven offensive weapons outside of Walker in what should be a low-scoring contest, I think Mike Macdonald and Co. narrowly steal one to hand Kansas City its first loss. Tyler Brown: This one has the look of a defensive rock fight. Seattle’s passing defense ranks first in the NFL, allowing just 141 yards per game, and Kansas City’s defense has held opponents under 20 points in most of its wins. The ingredients are there for a low-scoring grind from start to finish. That said, the Chiefs are the number one offense in the NFL for a reason. Seattle’s defense may be able to slow down Walker or Mahomes, but doing both simultaneously is a different ask entirely. If the run game gets going, the play-action attack opens up. away.headline: When will Rashee Rice come back to the Chiefs?
away.blurb: Entering a big Sunday night road matchup against the Seattle Seahawks , the Kansas City Chiefs kind of seem ... better than ever? At the very least, with a 5-0 undefeated record, it sure seems like the Chiefs have regained their place as a bona fide AFC heavyweight. Patrick Mahomes is playing some exemplary football, Kenneth Walker III is the NFL's premier running back right now, and a stingy defense is often dictating the terms of engagement. Unfortunately for the Chiefs, as they get set to face the Seahawks' similarly great defense, they're going to have to do it without one of their best downfield weapons. Veteran receiver Rashee Rice will not play on Sunday night as he continues recovering from a hamstring injury suffered in early October. For a Chiefs team sorely lacking reliable receivers on the outside, Rice's absence could be glaring against Seattle's pass-rush and secondary: As for when Rice might come back to the Chiefs, it wouldn't be shocking to see him play on the road against the Denver Broncos next Sunday. That would give the playmaker roughly a month to recover from his injury, which should be enough since his hamstring strain didn't appear too severe at first glance. The Chiefs do have a bye week in three weeks, but that seems like an unnecessarily lengthy absence for Rice if he's ready to roll soon. And he probably should be, barring more precautions. Who is Rashee Rice's backup on the Chiefs? Cyrus Allen is listed as Rice's backup on the Chiefs' official depth chart. Allen is a rookie who was selected in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. home.blurb: Travis Kelce's first injury scare of the 2026 NFL season has put Kansas City Chiefs fans on alert ahead of their Week 7 clash with the Seattle Seahawks. The veteran tight end appeared on the injury report with an ankle issue after a strong start to his 14th season. However, the latest update brings encouraging news for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. With Kansas City aiming to extend its unbeaten run, Kelce's availability could make a significant difference to the team's passing attack, particularly with another key offensive weapon ruled out. Kelce first appeared on the injury report on Wednesday with an ankle injury. He participated in practice on a limited basis that day and remained limited during Thursday and Friday's sessions. Although the repeated limitations raised concerns about his availability, the team did not assign him an official game designation. The matchup is important for Kansas City, which entered Week 7 with a 5-0 record after beating the Los Angeles Chargers 22-6. The Chiefs will want their experienced tight end available as they look to maintain their perfect start against a Seahawks team led by quarterback Sam Darnold. Those numbers highlight why his availability matters. Kelce gives Mahomes a trusted target who can turn short passes into significant gains. His experience and ability to find space in coverage also help the quarterback keep drives alive when deeper options are unavailable. However, Kansas City will have to manage the absence of wide receiver Rashee Rice, who has been ruled out with hamstring and knee injuries. Offensive lineman Jaylon Moore is also unavailable because of a concussion. Kansas City faces the Seahawks on Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET before preparing for a Week 8 AFC West showdown against the Denver Broncos. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have listed five players on their injury report ahead of Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks . Three players have been ruled out, while two remain questionable for the matchup. Chiefs rule out players as others remain questionable According to the Kansas City Chiefs , five players are listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks. L'Jarius Sneed and Cooper McDonald are questionable, while Rashee Rice, Jaylon Moore and Brashard Smith are out. Left tackle Josh Simmons was previously placed on injured reserve with a back injury . Sneed and McDonald are both dealing with knee injuries. Sneed was limited in practice throughout the week, leaving his availability for the game against Seattle uncertain. McDonald is also listed as questionable because of his knee injury. He was designated to return from injured reserve on October 20 and has participated in limited practices since then. Moore has been ruled out because of a concussion. The offensive tackle missed practice while dealing with the injury, creating an opening along the offensive line. Joshua Ezeudu is a possible replacement at right tackle. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has practiced fully and does not carry an injury designation for the game. Tight end Travis Kelce was limited in practice because of an ankle issue, but he also has no game designation. Both players are available for Sunday night's matchup. Rice, Moore and Smith have been ruled out, while Sneed and McDonald are listed as questionable. Kansas City will face Seattle at Lumen Field on Sunday night, with Kelce available despite limited participation in practice. home.headline: Week 7 Injury Report: Chiefs at Seahawks
home.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). For the Chiefs, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper Macdonald (knee) are both listed as questionable after being limited in Friday's practice. Kansas City's injury report featured only two changes from Wednesday. Running back Brashard Smith was added to the report, listed as limited with a hamstring injury, while left tackle Josh Simmons (back) was removed from the report because he was placed on injured reserve on Thursday. That means that for the second day in a row, right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring, knee) did not practice. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their final injury report ahead of Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs haven't been at full strength on the offensive line all season, and in recent weeks the injury bug has also hit the wide receiver position. With RT Jaylon Moore (concussion) and WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) ruled out, that will remain the case in Week 7's game on “Sunday Night Football.” That means more opportunities for players like WR Andrew Armstrong , OT Joshua Ezeudu, and even OT Diego Pounds . KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related With Jaylon Moore ruled out, Joshua Ezeudu is in line for his first start in Kansas City . With Rashee Rice ruled out, expect that Andrew Armstrong will be relied upon again in some capacity, whether activated to the 53-man roster via standard elevation or full promotion. CB L'Jarius Sneed was listed as questionable last week and still played. TE Travis Kelce carries no game status despite three consecutive limited practices. Seahawks HC Mike McDonald says that RB Zach Charbonnet did not suffer a setback and that ruling him out was “part of the plan.” Seahawks starting OG Anthony Bradford carries no game status and should return to the starting lineup. Linebacker remains a position where Seattle is very thin after ruling out Drake Thomas and Chazz Surratt. Expect practice squad elevations at that position. home.blurb: On Thursday, Kansas City placed left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) on the Reserve/Injured list after he didn’t practice on Wednesday. The Chiefs explained that Simmons plateaued in his rehabilitation and needed more time to return to 100%. For more information from the team’s Head Trainer Rick Burkholder, we covered his statement to local media here . Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) did not participate in practice again after entering the concussion protocol during the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Moore’s participation going forward is dependent on the contracted independent neurologist and completely out of the team and player’s hands. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a limited participant in practice again. Kelce briefly left in Week 6 against the Chargers and was seen multiple times having his ankle taped. Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) was a limited participant in practice for the second straight day. McDonald was placed on the team’s Reserve/Injured list after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Although he has been “designated to return,” McDonald must be officially added to the active roster by Saturday in order to play against Seattle. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday. Veteran defensive end Demarcus Lawrence (non-injury related - rest) was a limited participant in practice on Thursday after sitting out on Wednesday. Starting outside linebacker Uchenne Nwosu (hip) popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant after not appearing on the list on Wednesday. Former Missouri quarterback, the backup to Sam Darnold, Drew Lock (right elbow) was a limited participant in practice on both days this week. Wide receiver Rasheed Shaheed (hip), linebacker Tyrice Knight, and guards Anthony Bradford (knee) and Beau Stephens (knee) were full participants in Thursday’s practice after limited action on Wednesday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys. Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender Skip to main content SI.COM As if everything else that has gone wrong for the Dallas Cowboys' defense hasn't been enough, the unit has also been ravaged by injuries to make matters worse. The Cowboys are missing starters at cornerback, safety and linebacker, and now they are in danger of losing yet another linebacker from the starting lineup. home.headline: Eagles list 24 on injury report as Smith, Wicks and Goedert sit out
home.blurb: Saquon Barkley’s return to practice gave the Eagles an encouraging sign Thursday, but another lengthy injury report raised concerns about their passing game ahead of Monday night’s matchup against Dallas. Philadelphia listed 24 players, including six who did not participate. DeVonta Smith sat out with a hamstring injury, Dontayvion Wicks was sidelined with an ankle injury, and Dallas Goedert did not practice because of a knee injury. Barkley was listed as limited with his hamstring injury after missing the past two games. NFL Network reported earlier Thursday that he was expected to practice and was in line to play against Dallas. Barkley has rushed for 182 yards on 36 carries this season, averaging 5.1 yards per attempt. Philadelphia also had eight limited participants, including Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Drew Kendall and Tyler Steen. Dickerson was listed with knee and pectoral injuries, while Hunt was listed with knee and ankle injuries. Their availability will be important as Philadelphia attempts to establish more consistency around quarterback Tanner McKee. Goedert added six receptions for 61 yards against the Panthers , making his status another significant storyline for an offense already operating without Jalen Hurts. Michael Carter, Willie Lampkin and Nolan Smith joined the three pass catchers as nonparticipants. Smith remains listed with a concussion after leaving against Carolina. Among the encouraging developments, Jordan Davis practiced fully after leaving Sunday’s game with shin and thumb injuries. Zack Baun, Marquise Brown, Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers also participated fully. Thursday’s report reflects practice participation, not final availability. Hurts missed this past Sunday's game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. He had previously played in a loss to the Jaguars in London earlier this month. "Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football," the team announced. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery." Hurts last played in a loss to the Jaguars in London. He threw for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reports that Hurts stayed up for about 36 hours straight before that game, after being diagnosed. "How committed is Jalen Hurts to football? home.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys.
